pharm: Beta-lactam (4th-gen cephalosporin); inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis
summary: Cefpirome is a parenteral fourth-generation cephalosporin with broad activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including many Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas. It is used for serious hospital infections such as severe pneumonia, complicated urinary tract infection, skin and soft-tissue infection, bacteraemia and infections in neutropenic patients. It is not FDA-approved; dosing follows European SmPC/BNF. The usual adult dose is 1-2 g IV every 12 hours, reduced in renal impairment.
indications: Severe lower respiratory tract infections (e.g., hospital-acquired pneumonia)
Complicated upper and lower urinary tract infections
Infections in neutropenic and immunocompromised patients

dosage.c: Complicated/severe UTI, skin and soft-tissue infection

dosage.d: Usual first dose, then 0.5-1 g every 12 hours
dosage.n: Further reduction for CrCl <20 mL/min and dialysis

admin: Reconstitute and give by slow IV injection (3-5 minutes) or short IV infusion (20-30 minutes)
Confirm renal function and adjust dose accordingly
Screen for penicillin/cephalosporin allergy before use
Use within recommended time after reconstitution
Reserve for serious infections to limit resistance
moa: Fourth-generation cephalosporin that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis; its zwitterionic structure gives rapid outer-membrane penetration and stability to many beta-lactamases, broadening activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive organisms.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to cefpirome or other cephalosporins
History of severe immediate hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to penicillins or other beta-lactams
relative: Renal impairment (dose adjustment and neurotoxicity risk)
History of gastrointestinal disease, particularly colitis

preg: Limited data; use only if clearly necessary. No teratogenicity signal in animal studies.
lact: Excreted in breast milk in small amounts; use with caution and monitor the infant for GI effects.
renal: Predominantly renally eliminated; reduce dose and/or extend interval according to creatinine clearance, with further reduction in dialysis patients.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment required for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Aminoglycosides and loop diuretics — additive nephrotoxicity; monitor renal function
Probenecid — may reduce renal clearance and raise cefpirome levels
interactions.alcohol: No specific disulfiram-like interaction reported (no relevant side chain).
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive direct Coombs test and false-positive urinary glucose with non-enzymatic (copper-reduction) tests.

serious: Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures), particularly in renal impairment
Severe cutaneous reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)

monitoring: Renal function (dose adjustment and neurotoxicity risk)
Signs of hypersensitivity, especially early in therapy
Diarrhea during and after treatment (C. difficile)
Neurologic status in patients with renal impairment or high doses
counsel: This antibiotic is given by injection in hospital
Tell staff about any previous reaction to penicillins or cephalosporins
Report rash, swelling or breathing difficulty immediately
Report watery or bloody diarrhea, even after the course ends
pk: Store powder below 25 C; protect from light; use reconstituted solution promptly
pearls: Not FDA-approved; dosing and safety per European SmPC / BNF
Fourth-generation cephalosporin with antipseudomonal and broad Gram-positive/Gram-negative cover
Reduce dose in renal impairment to avoid neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, seizures)
Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy is possible — screen before use
Reserve for serious hospital infections, including febrile neutropenia, to limit resistance
missed: Administered on a fixed hospital schedule by staff; a delayed dose is given as soon as noticed and the schedule is adjusted by the team, not doubled.
overdose: Overdose, especially with renal impairment, may cause neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures). Provide supportive care, control seizures, and consider haemodialysis to remove the drug.
